newsitem.title: USA: Con Edison agrees to rate cuts - paper.
newsitem.headline: Con Edison agrees to rate cuts - paper.

text.p: Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc has reached an agreement with state regulators to reduce rates while phasing in retail competition over five years, The New York Times newspaper reported.

Citing a draft agreement between the utility and the staff of the New York Public Service Commission, the newspaper said the cuts are structured to provide the greatest rate relief for the utility's largest customers, manufacturers. Many of them have threatened to leave the state in search of lower- cost power, it said, referring to their influence as job providers.
The newspaper said the agreement between Con Edison and state regulators was not final.
Some utility officials said they thought the article was a trial balloon floated by New York Governor George Pataki's office.
Con Edison spokesman Richard Mulieri declined to talk about the terms discussed in the article.
Mulieri said the utility expected to reach an agreement with the commission and was surprised when the deadline for filings with the commission was extended last week to March 10.
Con Edison had sought a one-week extention to March 7, he said.
In its original filing last September, the utility had proposed a rate freeze during the transition period. It also said it supported securitization of stranded assets.
Securitization would allow Con Edison to cut rates immediately, Mulieri said.

With a Republican governor and representatives in control of the state Senate, Democratic assembly speaker Sheldon Silver has blocked securitization until he can get a role in the utility deregulation process, the newspaper said.
It said estimates of borrowing under a securitization program in New York state ranged as high $32 billion.
